name: Kistefos
overview: Industrial museum, sculpture park and contemporary art museum at Kistefossveien 112 in Jevnaker, on the Randselva river (stated by the museum).

The wood pulp mill on the site was founded in 1889 by Anders Sveaas and produced pulp until the mid-1950s. His grandson Christen Sveaas set up the museum in 1996 (stated by the museum). Wikipedia says Sveaas bought the company back in 1993 and acquired 85 percent of it in 1995 with the aim of creating an industrial museum and a contemporary sculpture park.
The original machinery and buildings are kept as a "Living Factory" (stated by the museum).
funding_verdict: Kistefos: owner-funded: the founder Christen Sveaas through his company Kistefos AS and his foundations, with state, municipal and savings-bank foundation grants

name: Esplanade, Theatres on the Bay
overview: A performing arts centre at 1 Esplanade Drive, Singapore, with a Theatre, a Concert Hall, studios, the Singtel Waterfront Theatre (550 seats), an Annexe Studio, an Outdoor Theatre and a Forecourt Garden (Esplanade website).
It opened officially on 12 October 2002 and is operated by The Esplanade Co Ltd, a not-for-profit registered charity (Esplanade website).

What is there: the pages read name the venues and describe Esplanade as a presenter and commissioner of festivals and series (for example Huayi, Pesta Raya), and name no resident companies and no collection (Esplanade website, annual report FY2019/20).
funding_verdict: Esplanade, Theatres on the Bay: mainly public, with government grants, a government rental subvention, mall rents and sponsors

name: Singapore Art Museum
overview: Contemporary art museum of Singapore, presenting art from a Southeast Asian perspective. Its main venue is Tanjong Pagar Distripark, 39 Keppel Road, and it also shows work in partner spaces across the island (Roots, Singapore Art Museum).
It opened to the public on 20 October 1995 and was officially opened by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on 20 January 1996 (Wikipedia).
The original home is the former St Joseph's Institution on Bras Basah Road, built in 1855 and now a National Monument (Roots). Restoring it took more than two years and cost S$30 million (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Singapore Art Museum: Visual Arts Cluster governance with ministry and National Arts Council seats on the board, plus named private, corporate and foreign cultural donors

name: National Asian Culture Center (ACC)
overview: State-run arts complex, also called the Asia Culture Center, at 38 Munhwajeondang-ro, Dong-gu, Gwangju. It belongs to the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (the centre's own site).
Built between 2008 and 2014 under a plan finalised in 2007 (the centre's own site). It opened in November 2015 (Wikipedia). Seoul Shinmun dated the partial opening to 4 September 2015.

Seoul Shinmun (2015) says the complex was built on the site of the former South Jeolla Provincial Office. Wikipedia says the final design kept the above-ground buildings and added underground ones, and that the centre pays tribute to the 1980 Gwangju Uprising.
funding_verdict: National Asian Culture Center (ACC): mainly public: South Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism
wider_context: Wikipedia says the choice of Gwangju was disputed because the city has no historic links to heritage sites or cultural significance related to art, that construction was delayed for several years by complaints from the local community, and that residents, families of victims and May 18 Democratization Movement organisations felt the project did not honour the original promises of preserving the movement's legacy.
Seoul Shinmun says the complex was built on the former South Jeolla Provincial Office site, and Newsis says May 18 groups demanded preservation of its annex.

press_items.title: Kang Hyun-kyung, "Culture Hub Plan Losing Money" (2008)
Ryu Hyeong-geun, "Also Discussed at Gwangju City Parliamentary Audit... Seeking Ways to Revitalize the Asia Culture Center" (25 October 2018, title translated)

name: Fundación MAPFRE
overview: Exhibition halls at Paseo de Recoletos 23 in Madrid, of about 1,000 square metres, run by the culture area of Fundación MAPFRE, which also runs the KBr photography centre in Barcelona, opened in autumn 2020 (foundation website).

Fundación MAPFRE is a non-profit institution created by the insurer Mapfre, constituted on 5 November 1975 and classed as a private cultural foundation by the Ministry of Education and Science on 14 May 1976; its registered office is at Paseo de Recoletos 23 (annual accounts 2025).

What is there: three seasons a year of paired exhibitions of painting and photography, on international art from the mid 19th to the mid 20th century and on photographers of the 20th century and the present; the 2025 exhibitions in Madrid had 319,559 visitors (annual accounts 2025). The foundation's own collections hold more than 2,000 pieces, mainly drawings, prints and photographs, with photography added from 2007 (foundation website); the balance sheet carries them under 'Museos' at 20,360 thousand euros net, and 2025 purchases of 300 thousand euros went mainly on photographs by Eduardo Nave, María Linarejos, Jorge Yeregui, Paula Artés and Israel Ariño (annual accounts 2025).
funding_verdict: Fundación MAPFRE: private, paid from dividends of the insurer Mapfre S.A., which the foundation controls

name: Museo Picasso Málaga
aliases: Fundación Museo Picasso Málaga. Legado Paul, Christine y Bernard Ruiz-Picasso
overview: A museum of Pablo Picasso's work in the Palacio de Buenavista, a sixteenth-century palace in the old centre of Málaga, extended with new buildings by Richard Gluckman with Cámara Martín Delgado Arquitectos (museum website).

Opened on 27 October 2003; it is managed by the Fundación Museo Picasso Málaga. Legado Paul, Christine y Bernard Ruiz-Picasso, the private foundation that owns the collection, the museum's assets and the palace (museum website).

The core of the collection is the 233 works donated by Christine and Bernard Ruiz-Picasso, complemented by pieces from the Fundación Almine y Bernard Ruiz-Picasso (FABA) and other loans; under the palace is an archaeological site with Phoenician and Roman remains (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Picasso Málaga: half visitors, a third regional grant, in a family foundation with the Junta de Andalucía on its board

name: CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo
aliases: centro de arte dos de mayo
CA2M (Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo)
overview: Contemporary art museum at Avenida de la Constitución 23 in central Móstoles, in the Comunidad de Madrid (Es Madrid).
Opened in May 2008 on the site of a traditional building called La Casona (Spanish Wikipedia).

Building of 5,886 square metres with exhibition rooms on three floors, a 100-seat auditorium, a library and a terrace. The basic architectural project is by Celia Vinuesa, executed by Pablo Pérez-Urruti, and since 2016 Andrés Jaque Studio, Office for Political Innovation, has carried out a series of "architectural acupuncture" interventions (Es Madrid).
funding_verdict: CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo: public: Comunidad de Madrid (regional government)

name: Usine Kugler (Fédération des Artistes de Kugler)
overview: Former tap factory in the Jonction area of Geneva, now artists' studios and exhibition and performance spaces. The Fonderie Kugler is at Avenue de la Jonction 19, 1205 Geneva (guide-contemporain.ch).

The Fédération des artistes de Kugler (FAK) is the federation of the artist associations based at the site: Kugler Est, Atelier Drozophile, Cheminée Nord, Espace Kugler, Kuglof, La Database59, L-Ouest, L-Sud and Verrière Sud (usinekugler.ch).

The Fonderie Kugler sits alongside about 220 active professional artists' studios, keeps its industrial architecture and has a 400 m2 modular space for artistic research and emerging arts. It is managed collectively through an office and run by the FAK (guide-contemporain.ch).
funding_verdict: Usine Kugler: self-managed artist federation; public bodies handle the site and list the Fonderie

name: Plateforme 10
overview: Plateforme 10 is an arts district beside Lausanne station that brings together, in the site's words, 3 canton-level museums and 2 foundations: the Musée cantonal des beaux-arts (MCBA), mudac and Photo Elysée (site).

The MCBA building was inaugurated in 2019; Photo Elysée and mudac moved in during 2022, and the site opened to the public on the weekend of 19 June 2022 with 30,000 visits across 25,000 square metres (site; Canton of Vaud press release).
What is there: the MCBA's permanent display includes some three hundred works from the eighteenth century to the present; the pages read gave no collection figures for mudac or Photo Elysée.
funding_verdict: Plateforme 10: public-private, the Canton of Vaud with private donors; operating funding not stated on the pages read

name: Montreux Jazz Festival
aliases: Claude Nobs Collection of the Montreux Jazz Festival
overview: The Montreux Jazz Festival has been held since 1967; its collection has brought together 5,000 concerts since then (EPFL).
Claude Nobs was its founder and director (EPFL).
What is there: the archive holds over 11,000 hours of video and 6,000 hours of audio, including multitrack, digitised and stored in three copies (EPFL).
funding_verdict: Montreux Jazz Festival: festival funding not stated on the pages read; archive paid for by named donors led by Audemars Piguet

name: Opernhaus Zürich
overview: The Opernhaus Zürich is a company, Opernhaus Zürich AG, with offices at Falkenstrasse 1, 8008 Zürich (media release).

What is there: in 2024/25 it held 314 performances for about 226,000 visitors at 87.2% occupancy; the cantonal report names Serebrennikov, Andreas Homoki's farewell Elias and Cathy Marston's ballet Clara, and the journal Opernwelt named it Opernhaus des Jahres 2025 (Regierungsrat decision 440, 2026).
General music director is Gianandrea Noseda and ballet director Cathy Marston; Homoki's Ring des Nibelungen was staged in 2023/24 (media release, 17 December 2024).
funding_verdict: Opernhaus Zürich: mainly public, Kanton Zürich contributions of CHF 91.351 million in 2023/24, plus sponsors, donations and ticket sales

name: Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich
overview: The Tonhalle Zürich is run by the Tonhalle-Gesellschaft Zürich AG, one of six major cultural institutions of Zürich and Winterthur eligible for cantonal Kulturfonds contributions (Regierungsrat decision 709, 24 June 2026).
Music director is Paavo Järvi; the Tonhalle plans a Beethoven programme for the 200th anniversary of his death in 2027 with choir works, chamber music and participation formats (decision 709).
What is there: the pages read gave no collection or repertoire list.
funding_verdict: Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich: public (city and canton); the canton's lottery fund gave CHF 1,872,000 in project money for 2023 to 2027

name: Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts
overview: Municipal art museum in Gushan District, Kaohsiung, set in the Neiweipi Cultural Park. Wikipedia gives the museum about 33,000 square metres and 1994 as its year of establishment.

Founded by the Kaohsiung City Government. Wikipedia reports that the Kaohsiung Bureau of Cultural Affairs has administered it since 2003. The museum's own sponsorship page says it became an administrative corporation in 2017.
Building: Wikipedia says the galleries span four floors and that sunlight reaches the Sculpture Hall through a large skylight.
funding_verdict: Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts: city-founded administrative corporation, with named corporate, foundation and individual sponsors

press_items.title: Song Yuan-chang (宋原彰), "孩童模仿畢卡索真跡遭制止引眾怒 高美館緊急改規定：開放速寫" (17 August 2024; title translated: child copying a Picasso original stopped sparks outrage, museum urgently changes rules to allow sketching)

name: Museum of Anatolian Civilizations
overview: Archaeology museum on the south side of Ankara Castle in the Atpazarı area of Ulus, Ankara (Wikipedia; Turkish Museums, Ministry of Culture and Tourism).
Began in 1921 when the culture director Mübarek Galip set up a museum in the Akkale bastion of the castle, at Atatürk's wish for a Hittite museum (Turkish Museums).

Housed in two Ottoman buildings, the Mahmut Paşa Bedesteni (covered bazaar) and the Kurşunlu Han, which the Culture and Tourism Minister dates to the reign of Mehmed II; the central hall opened to visitors in 1943, during the conversion (Turkish Museums; DHA, 21 July 2026).
funding_verdict: Museum of Anatolian Civilizations: state: Turkey's Ministry of Culture and Tourism
wider_context: A Court of Accounts (Sayıştay) audit found that the museum's asset codes for its objects did not match its inventory register, so a physical count could not easily locate an object, and that its storerooms lacked suitable size, temperature, light and humidity conditions (Sözcü, 2 October 2021).

name: Istanbul Archaeology Museums
overview: Complex of three museums in one garden on the Osman Hamdi Bey slope between Gülhane Park and Topkapı Palace, Sultanahmet, Fatih: the Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient and the Tiled Kiosk (Turkish Museums, Ministry of Culture and Tourism).

Founded in 1869 as the Müze-i Hümayun (Imperial Museum) from antiquities gathered in Hagia Irene; Osman Hamdi Bey became director in 1881 and brought the Sidon royal necropolis sarcophagi to Istanbul after his 1887 to 1888 excavations (Turkish Museums).

Buildings: the Tiled Kiosk of 1472, built under Mehmed II and a museum since 1880; Alexandre Vallaury's 1883 Academy of Fine Arts building, the Museum of the Ancient Orient since 1917; and Vallaury's neo-classical Archaeological Museum, opened in 1891 (Turkish Museums).
funding_verdict: Istanbul Archaeology Museums: state: Turkey's Ministry of Culture and Tourism

name: Sadler's Wells
overview: Sadler's Wells runs four London venues: Sadler's Wells Theatre and the Lilian Baylis Studio at Angel, the Peacock Theatre in the West End and Sadler's Wells East in Stratford (museum website).

The Angel theatre is the sixth on its site and the first opened in 1683; the Mayor of London opened Sadler's Wells East on 6 February 2025 as part of East Bank (museum website; Sadler's Wells East page).
What is there: a dance house that presents productions in its theatres and on tour, with a Digital Stage; the Trust's theatre presentations earned £23,110k in 2024-25 (museum website; accounts 2025).
funding_verdict: Sadler's Wells: earned income, Arts Council England and a growing donor and sponsor income, with public capital money behind Sadler's Wells East
wider_context: East Bank is the Mayor of London's cultural and education district in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park; East Bank is the Mayor's culture and education district, with Sadler's Wells East a partner alongside the BBC, UAL's London College of Fashion, UCL and the V&A (Sadler's Wells East page; Mayor of London press release).

name: Harry Ransom Center
overview: A humanities research library and museum at 300 West 21st Street on the UT Austin campus; the current building opened in 1972 and a $14.5 million renovation was completed in 2003 (HRC website).
Founded in 1957 by Harry Huntt Ransom, an English professor who later became chancellor of UT, as the Humanities Research Center (HRC website).

What is there: about 1 million books, more than 42 million manuscripts, 5 million photographs and 100,000 works of art. Named holdings include one of only 20 complete Gutenberg Bibles, Gabriel Garcia Marquez's manuscripts, correspondence and notebooks, digitized for viewing, and the Gernsheim Collection on the history of photography, acquired in 1963 (HRC website).
funding_verdict: Harry Ransom Center: mainly public, through the state university, plus endowment and private gifts
wider_context: In an opinion piece in the Austin American-Statesman on 10 March 2017, the Center's director, Stephen Enniss, wrote about the proposed elimination of the National Endowment for the Arts and the National Endowment for the Humanities, according to the Center's magazine (Ransom Center Magazine, 23 March 2017). The page read did not give the text of the argument.

name: Buffalo AKG Art Museum
overview: An art museum at 1285 Elmwood Avenue, Buffalo, in the Jeffrey E. Gundlach Building by OMA, linked by the John J. Albright Bridge to the historic Albright and Knox buildings; the renovated museum opened on 12 June 2023 as the Buffalo AKG Art Museum (annual report FY2023; museum website).

Founded in December 1862 as the Buffalo Fine Arts Academy, with former President Millard Fillmore among its incorporators; John J. Albright paid for the first permanent home, dedicated on 31 May 1905, and Seymour H. Knox Jr. and his family led gifts for the Gordon Bunshaft wing that opened in January 1962 (museum website, Our History).

What is there: the museum says it has acquired more than 5,000 artworks since 1962. Named works and gifts include Albert Bierstadt's The Marina Piccola, Capri (1859), its first artwork in 1863; Picasso's La Toilette (1906); Clyfford Still's gift of 31 paintings in 1964; and Marisol's 2016 bequest of her whole estate. Other major contributors to the collection include A. Conger Goodyear, Dorothy and Herbert Vogel and Giuseppe Panza di Biumo (museum website, Our History).
funding_verdict: Buffalo AKG Art Museum: mainly private, through one very large donor and matching campaign, with county, city and state money

name: Cincinnati Art Museum
overview: An art museum at 953 Eden Park Drive in Eden Park, Cincinnati, Ohio (museum website).
The Cincinnati Museum Association was incorporated on 15 February 1881 to build and run it, and it opened on 17 May 1886 (museum website).
The collection is more than 73,000 works covering 6,000 years, searchable online (museum website).
funding_verdict: Cincinnati Art Museum: private gifts and endowment return, with city, state and ArtsWave operating support

name: The Cleveland Orchestra
overview: A symphony orchestra of more than 100 members that plays year round at Severance Music Center, 11001 Euclid Ave, at Blossom Music Center, on tour and in residencies in Miami and Vienna (orchestra website).
It is run by The Musical Arts Association, whose records the orchestra's archive holds (orchestra website, Archives). The pages read did not give the founding year.

What is there: Franz Welser-Moest is the orchestra's seventh and longest-serving music director, and 2026 to 2027 is his 25th and final season; the orchestra issues recordings including a vinyl box set (orchestra website).
funding_verdict: The Cleveland Orchestra: mainly private gifts and endowment, with a county cigarette-tax grant
wider_context: The public grant is paid from a tax on cigarettes that Ideastream reported was declining, which cut the 2014 round by about 6.5 percent; the 2025 and 2026 grant lists show the orchestra's grant at $863,659 and then $1,000,000 (Ideastream, 25 November 2014; CAC grant lists).
